source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Astika sub-parva, end of adhyaya 29 and adhyaya 30: Indra strikes Garuda with the vajra; Garuda, unhurt, laughing, speaks gently: he honours the sage from whose bones the vajra was made, and the vajra, and Indra, and lets fall a single feather; seeing its beauty, all beings name him Suparna, 'the fine-feathered'. Indra, amazed, asks for his friendship and to know the measure of his strength; Garuda answers that he could carry the earth with its mountains, forests and oceans, and Indra with it, on a single feather. Indra asks for the soma back; Garuda says he is taking it for a purpose and will let no one drink it: where he sets it down, Indra may take it. Indra, pleased, offers a boon, and Garuda asks that the mighty serpents be his food. (The cliffhanger: he flies down, and Indra follows unseen.)

lines.text: "I honour the sage whose bones made this weapon. I honour you. Here is one feather."

lines.speaker: garuda
